title: Activation Nexus — Roadmap Cheatsheet & KPI Sprint Docket
body:
Purpose:
A compact operational cheat-sheet intended to sit next to the launch board during the first 14 days of a phased rollout. This doc pairs a lightweight roadmap with the sprint-level KPI docket and a short, prioritized readiness checklist that is deliberately minimal — enough to make go/no-go decisions and rapid mitigations without overwhelming the commander station.

Audience:
- Product Ops lead (primary)
- Release engineer, infra oncall, SRE, applied ML lead, growth PM

How to use:
- Keep this file pinned in the launch channel and on the console 'Go-live' tab.
- Update KPI snapshot daily (top section) and annotate any outliers with a 1-line hypothesis.
- Use the binary health strip (green/amber/red) to make immediate traffic/fallback moves.

Sprint docket (14-day window):
- Day 0 (canary): 1% traffic, all new model variants behind feature-flag. Validate p95 latency and error < 0.5%.
- Day 1–3 (probe): 1–10% traffic, warm caches, observe guidance from runtime on batch sizes.
- Day 4–7 (ramp): 10–50% traffic, run targeted A/B on quantized variant if cost delta > 30% and quality delta < 0.5%.
- Day 8–14 (scale): >50% traffic if stability gates pass. Maintain at least one cross-traffic fallback route.

Daily checklist (5 minute quick-run):
- Is p95 latency within target? (Y/N) — measure across region + model variant
- Any error-rate spikes > 2x baseline? (Y/N)
- Cost-per-1k trending above forecast by >15%? (Y/N)
- Quality drift flagged by eval sets? (Y/N)
- Cache hit-rate below 25%? (Y/N)
- All oncall owners acknowledged morning post? (Y/N)

Binary health strip (single-line summary):
- Green: all daily checks NO except permissible variance flags (latency within 10% of target). Proceed with planned ramp.
- Amber: any one daily check is YES and needs immediate mitigation steps (see triggers). Hold traffic increases; run micro-rollforward tests.
- Red: multiple checks failing or a single severe P0 (e.g., sustained p99 latency > 2x target, or quality-regression > 0.5%). Roll back to last known-good model, open incident.

Immediate mitigation triggers (short-form):
- p95 latency > 2x target for 10+ minutes -> pause ramp, shift 30% traffic to fallback-region or older model, increase infra autoscale cap, notify SRE.
- Error rate > 5% absolute increase -> cut traffic by 50%, disable async-hyperbatch, enable degraded-mode prompts, page oncall.
- Cost-per-1k > forecast + 25% -> switch to quantized variant for non-critical cohorts, throttle sampling rate for heavy eval routes.
- Quality regression delta > 0.3% (measured on pre-defined eval set) -> halt rollout for affected cohort, start immediate A/B with old model for 10k requests.

Owner map (fast lookup):
- Product Ops: Maria Chen — launch coordination, scoreboard owner
- Serving Runtime: Oliver Park — cache tuning, batch knobs
- SRE: Samir Joshi — latency, error triage, rollback authority
- Applied ML: Lina Gómez — quality checks, eval set ownership
- Finance: Priya Ramaswamy — cost tracking and alerting

Communication template for channel when a flag trips (copy/paste):
[ALERT] Day {D} | {metric} breached | current={value} target={target} | action={action taken} | owner={owner} | next-step={next-step}

Lightweight risk register (keep top 6 risks only):
- Risk: cold-cache p95 spike on regional failover. Mitigation: warm caches pre-ramp using synthetic traffic + staggered region switchover.
- Risk: quantized variant quality drop for low-frequency tokens. Mitigation: selective routing (high-value cohorts to full-precision variant).
- Risk: billing anomaly due to misconfigured autoscale. Mitigation: finance alert + cap queued autoscale for first 48h.
- Risk: observability gaps for function/tool calls in streaming responses. Mitigation: add tracing hook and run smoke for function paths.
- Risk: customer data path audit delay for private deployments. Mitigation: gate private beta until audit completed.
- Risk: rollout fatigue (too many micro-rollouts). Mitigation: consolidate minor changes into weekly bundles.

Notes on telemetry and quick evals:
- Primary eval set: prodops_activation_v1 (2000 prompts sampled daily). Run paired A/B quality tests every 3h during ramp.
- Synthetic traffic: 10% of canary load shaped to worst-case length distribution to validate kv-cache behavior.

Attachments / artifacts to check pre-go:
- Runtime perf matrix (linked) — expected p95 by seq length and model variant.
- Eval set diffs (linked) — last 4 runs annotated.
- Cost forecast + throttle schedule (linked)

Bottom-line decision rubric (one-line):
- Proceed with ramp if: p95 <= target, error-rate <= baseline*2, quality delta <= 0.15%, and cache-hit >= 20%. Any single hard-fail moves to amber/red protocol.

Revision history (summary):
- 2025-01-15 created initial baseline by Maria Chen.
- 2025-01-22 added quantized-routing notes (Lina Gómez).
- 2025-02-10 tightened p95 thresholds after infra perf run (Oliver Park).

Comfort notes for the commander: 
- This doc assumes you can flip traffic and toggle model variants within 5 minutes via the console. If that capability is absent, add "operator escalation" as additional owner and keep human roll-forward window of 20 minutes.

next_steps: 1) Validate console traffic toggle end-to-end (infra) by 2025-02-12. 2) Schedule a 30-min dry-run with SRE + runtime on 2025-02-14. 3) Freeze non-critical model changes 48h prior to canary. 4) Publish this doc to the go-live channel after final signoff.
notes_short: Designed to be minimalist and actionable. Keep it current; prune old mitigation entries after 30 days. If used for private deployments, ensure runbook has KMS/HSM owner appended.
